claim:
For every real \(\lambda>0\), let \(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\) be \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
N_\lambda(x,y)=\left(\|(x,y)\|_1^2+\lambda\|(x,y)\|_\infty^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Put
\[
M_\lambda=\frac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}2,
\qquad
m_\lambda=
\begin{cases}
1+\lambda,&0<\lambda\le2,\\
(\lambda+4)/2,&\lambda\ge2.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
d_{\mathrm{BM}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)},\ell_2^2\right)^2
=
\frac{M_\lambda}{m_\lambda}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}{2(1+\lambda)},&0<\lambda\le2,\\[2mm]
\dfrac{\lambda+2+\sqrt{\lambda^2+4}}{\lambda+4},&\lambda\ge2.
\end{cases}
\]
This is exactly the published Jordan--von Neumann constant of the same family, so
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
=
d_{\mathrm{BM}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)},\ell_2^2\right)^2
=
C_{\mathrm{NJ}}\!\left(Z_{1,\infty}^{(\lambda)}\right)
\qquad(\lambda>0).
\]

correctness.rationale: Signed-permutation symmetry reduces the Euclidean comparison globally to Q_lambda(t)=[lambda+(1+t)^2]/(1+t^2) on 0<=t<=1. Its derivative has the unique zero t_lambda=(sqrt(lambda^2+4)-lambda)/2, yielding the exact maximum M_lambda and an endpoint minimum m_lambda with a transition at lambda=2. Euclidean Ptolemy gives C_Pt<=M_lambda/m_lambda. Exact triples attain this ratio in both regimes. For the Banach--Mazur part, averaging any candidate quadratic form over the full signed-permutation isometry group preserves its comparison constants and forces a scalar Euclidean form, proving global affine optimality.
risks: The theorem does not depend on the published C_NJ formula for its Ptolemy or Banach--Mazur proof; that formula is used only to identify the three-way coincidence.

value.rationale: The cross-exponent region was explicitly identified as unresolved in the closest full-text Ptolemy literature. The endpoint p=1, q=infinity is canonical, not an arbitrary parameter slice, and the result treats every lambda>0 with a genuine phase transition at lambda=2. It also links three standard planar invariants through one exact comparison geometry and supplies explicit extremizers in both phases.
risks: The contribution is an endpoint-family theorem rather than a classification of the entire cross-exponent region.
